prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website homepage direction comp
Primary request: Create exactly one polished 1440x960 landscape desktop browser first viewport for VIZ Creative, an Abuja interior-design and architectural-visualization studio. It must read as a premium, usable real website—not a poster, moodboard, architectural drawing sheet, or generic portfolio grid.

Page structure: A slim 58px top navigation on a warm limewash background. At left, a restrained wordmark rendered exactly as "VIZ Creative". At right, small navigation labels rendered exactly as "WORK", "STUDIO", "PROCESS", "CONTACT". Below, create a bright architectural-section composition occupying the first viewport. A single fully visible 16:9 architectural render is centered and visually dominant, shown edge-to-edge within its own rectangular frame with the entire image visible and no cropping. The render depicts an inhabited contemporary Abuja residence as a sectional interior in clear daylight: shaded lounge, reading nook, textured limewash walls, restrained dark section-cut elements, planted courtyard, and a warm sunbeam tracing across the floor. Use photoreal architectural visualization inside the render, with believable material texture and a subtle human presence at normal scale.

Layout and hierarchy: To the left of the dominant render, place a compact studio statement, never a huge headline. Render this text exactly, with clean line breaks and no extra copy: "INTERIORS SHAPED / BY LIGHT, PLACE / AND DAILY LIFE." Keep it modest, approximately 28–34px, aligned to the image. Across a continuous thin sectional baseline beneath the render and statement, add sparse, highly legible architectural annotations: "08:15", "13:40", "17:55", "RESIDENTIAL", "HOSPITALITY", "VISUALIZATION". Align one clear charcoal-and-gold action on this same baseline, rendered exactly as "START A PROJECT →". Include a small north arrow and minimal sun-path arc as subtle functional annotation, secondary to the website. At the bottom edge, show only a clean hint of the next story section with the text "SELECTED STORIES" and the top sliver of one large project image, indicating scroll continuation.

Style/medium: realistic shippable product UI screenshot, exact flat front-on desktop viewport, crisp editorial web typography, contemporary Swiss-influenced grid, restrained luxury, generous negative space, precise alignment. Typography modern and restrained; labels and annotations secondary but sharply legible. No browser chrome, no device frame, no perspective mockup.

Color palette: background #efeee7 warm limewash; primary text and section cuts #20252a charcoal; sunlight and action accent #e9b63f sunlit gold; shadows and fine annotations #7e93a7 shadow blue. Use these four colors faithfully and sparingly.

Materials/textures: subtle limewash wall grain, crisp charcoal section cuts, natural timber, quiet stone, transparent glazing, physically plausible sun path and cast shadows. Keep UI surfaces mostly flat and editorial; visual richness belongs inside the architectural render.

Composition/framing: exact 3:2 landscape canvas corresponding to 1440x960. Full-width website viewport. The single 16:9 render is the dominant central object and must remain completely visible without cropping. Compact statement sits left of it. Continuous baseline unifies timestamps, fit labels, and CTA. The next section is only hinted at below the fold.

Text (verbatim): "VIZ Creative", "WORK", "STUDIO", "PROCESS", "CONTACT", "INTERIORS SHAPED / BY LIGHT, PLACE / AND DAILY LIFE.", "08:15", "13:40", "17:55", "RESIDENTIAL", "HOSPITALITY", "VISUALIZATION", "START A PROJECT →", "SELECTED STORIES"

Constraints: Exactly one homepage direction and exactly one dominant architectural render. Strong desktop-web usability and hierarchy. All listed text should appear once, spelled correctly. No huge editorial headline. No invented testimonials, awards, press logos, statistics, project counts, or performance metrics. No blurry side fills. No decorative glassmorphism. No generic card grid. No multiple hero renders. No excessive blueprint lines. No poster framing. No oversized logo. No laptop/device mockup. No watermark. Avoid illegible microtext and avoid any additional text beyond the verbatim list.
